english.title: Master of ship fail to assist other ship and stay by it in case of collision
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the master of a

(A)_[United Kingdom ship,]_
(B)_[foreign ship in United Kingdom waters,]

namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), which was in collision with another ship, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER SHIP..), without reasonable excuse failed, so far as you could do so without danger to your own ship, crew and passengers, to render to the other ship, its master, crew and passengers such assistance as may have been practicable and necessary to save them from danger caused by the collision, and to stay by the other ship until you had ascertained that it had no need of further assistance
english.legislation: Contrary to 92(1)(a) and (4)(a) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
master of UK ship or foreign ship in UK waters
fail to render assistance to other ship in case of collision
and stay by it until ascertaining no further assistance required

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: If the master is a certified officer, an enquiry into his conduct may be held, amd his certificate cancelled or suspended - section 92(4)

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £50,000.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None
